conviction_note: The FY26 operating lines and the £60m EPRA-earnings target are already public (7 Sep trading update), so the move sits in what the release adds: Sept-30 NTA, a likely first FY27 earnings guide, the final dividend and capital allocation. A possible buyback under pressure from Saba (10.1%) and Mike Ashley (4.2%) is the upside. Refinancing cost after the 5 Nov Bank Rate rise and gilts at 19-year highs is the downside, so the two roughly cancel: abs 4.5 (full-year days moved +1.1/+3.5/+4.7/-4.4 in 2022-25) and p_up 51 give +0.09. The findings sum to -0.3; the two measurements agree that there is no edge.

findings.finding: Saba Capital has built a 10.14% economic interest (4.28% shares plus 5.86% swaps, threshold crossed 7 Oct 2026) and Mike Ashley holds 4.19%. Grainger's own 7 Sep update moved its buyback language forward ('we will continue to closely consider the use of surplus capital in light of share price performance, weighing up the returns between share buybacks and investment opportunities') with the stock at about 0.61x HY NTA. That raises the chance that the full-year results announce a buyback or an accelerated return of capital.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback precedent in the window. Saba's initial 5% disclosure moved the stock +4.2% (10 Jun 2026, per QuotedData/AIC); the October rise to 9-10% coincided with a run from 160p to 186p.
findings.why_not_priced: The stakes are public and part of the October rally was a re-rating on them, so most of the 'activist present' effect is priced. What is not priced is whether the board acts at this release. HY26 and the sponsored note both rank buybacks below deleveraging, and a priced-in buyback would show as the stock holding its October high; instead it is down 5% from 186.8p (5 Nov) to 176.7p. Sized small because the company's stated priority argues against an announcement.
findings.independence: Mike Ashley TR-1 4.187% (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/grainger--gri/holding-s-in-company/9550770, 5 May 2026); the sponsored Progressive note says 'share buybacks could be compelling at this share price' (https://corporate.graingerplc.co.uk/sites/graingerplc-corp/files/2026-08/GRI-ProgressiveResearch-Aug26.pdf)

findings.finding: Sept-30 valuations land after a further outward move in rates: the 10y gilt ended September just under 5.4% (a 19-year high) and Nationwide's September HPI fell 0.2% m/m (annual +0.8%, London +0.4% in Q3). That points to EPRA NTA below the HY 290p, as the HY's 'modest yield expansion' already cut it 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HY26 (14 May 2026): NTA -3% to 290p and the stock rose +0.97%. FY25 (20 Nov 2025): -4.35% on results 'a little below expectations' (Berenberg, per Sharecast snippet).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are public macro series, and the stock at about 0.61x HY NTA already trades as if NTA were far lower. This is a macro-to-company transmission with no company or counterparty statement behind it, so it is small. If it were fully unpriced the discount would have stayed near 50% while gilts sold off; instead the stock rallied through October.
findings.independence: Gilt level from Trading Economics (https://tradingeconomics.com/united-kingdom/government-bond-yield/news/588169, 30 Sep 2026), snippet_only

findings.finding: Since the 7 Sep reaffirmation of '35% earnings growth FY25-FY29 ... after fully absorbing higher interest rates', the Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4.0% on 5 Nov and 2y gilts went above 5%. Grainger's sponsored analyst puts its market-rate debt cost at 5.5-6.0% against a 3.2% average. That raises the risk that a first FY27 guide comes in soft or the FY29 £72m target is qualified.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Full-year days: 2022 +1.1%, 2023 +3.47%, 2024 +4.73%, 2025 -4.35% (Yahoo daily closes). In 2025 the targets were held but results were 'a little below'. Progressive cut FY27E in Aug 2026 for pipeline timing.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate move is public, but its effect on Grainger's FY27-29 path has not been restated by the company since 7 Sep, which predates the hike. The 5% fall from the 5 Nov high suggests the market is partly marking this already. Kept small because 97% of debt is hedged with a 4.6-year maturity (per Progressive), the 2033 facility extension cut costs by about £1m a year, and the company explicitly said the target absorbs higher rates.
findings.independence: Progressive note on market-rate finance costs of c.5.5-6.0% and 97% hedging (https://corporate.graingerplc.co.uk/sites/graingerplc-corp/files/2026-08/GRI-ProgressiveResearch-Aug26.pdf)

baseline_tension: The baseline leans +2.79 on a short-squeeze prior, but the short is 4.8% and flat, not building, and the activist-led capital-return upside is offset by rate-driven guidance risk; on balance the evidence does not support the lean.
language_note: The domestic RNS record on Investegate carried what the wire summaries did not: the exact Saba split (4.28% shares plus 5.86% swaps, 10.14% total at 7 Oct; the press reported '9.2%') and the precise 7 Sep wording on buybacks 'in light of share price performance'.
The issuer's own corporate site hosts the sponsored Progressive note (FY26E £60.5m, FY27E £62.0m, DPS 8.6p), the only sourceable bar; no independent broker preview surfaced in English searches.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' / first FY guide is a scheduled guidance event: abs_move_pct raised from 3.5 to 4.5 because a first FY27 guide is likely, and the guidance finding resized from -0.6 to -0.8 on the guidance scale.
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the NTA/gilt finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3.
'A finding about a number already told is worth 0': confirmed that the pre-released operating lines were rejected rather than filed.
'Understatement is the systematic error': p_up moved from 52 to 51 rather than shrinking the size; the net expectation stays near zero because the evidence is balanced.
